Claim 1 (currently amended): A gas generator comprising: a composition containing an alkali metal chlorate as an oxidizer provided at about 25-75 weight percent, and a carboxylic acid as a fuel provided at about 25-75 weight percent, said percentages stated by weight of the total composition; and a desiccant in operable communication with said composition, wherein said desiccant is selected to enhance the thermal stability of the gas generating composition.

Claim 2 (currently amended): The gas generator of claim 1 wherein said desiccant is mixed into said composition at about 10-35 weight percent of the total composition, wherein said mixing enhances the thermal stability of the composition.

Claim 3 (original): The gas generator of claim 1 wherein said desiccant is in vapor communication with, but physically separated from, said composition, and said desiccant is provided in amounts resulting in a mass differential of about -5.0 to 5.0% of the composition after heat aging at 107C for 400 hours. (Previously presented)

Claim 4 (currently amended): The gas generator of claim 1 wherein said composition contains an extrusion aid provided at about 0.1-10 weight percent of the total gas generant composition, wherein said extrusion aid is selected to improve the processability of the composition.

Claim 5 (original): The gas generator of claim 4 wherein said extrusion aid is selected from graphite, fumed silica, and mixtures thereof. (Previously presented)

Claim 6 (original): The gas generator of claim 1 wherein said alkali metal chlorate is potassium chlorate. (Previously presented)

Claim 7 (currently amended): The gas generator of claim 1 wherein said carboxylic acid is selected from tartaric acid and its isomers, succinic acid, glutamic acid, adipic acid, and mucic acid, and mixtures thereof, wherein said selection is based on their combustion properties.

Claim 8 (original): The gas generator of claim 1 wherein said carboxylic acid is DL-tartaric acid. (Previously presented)

Claim 9 (currently amended): A gas generating system comprising: a gas generator comprising a composition, said composition containing an alkali metal chlorate as an oxidizer provided at about 25-75 weight percent, and said composition further containing a carboxylic acid as a fuel provided at about 25-75 weight percent, said percentages stated by weight of the total gas generant composition; and a desiccant in operable communication with said composition, wherein said desiccant is selected to enhance the thermal stability of the gas generating system.

Claim 10 (currently amended): The gas generating system of claim 9 wherein said desiccant is mixed into said composition at about 10-35 weight percent of the total composition, wherein said mixing enhances the thermal stability of the system.

Claim 11 (original): The gas generating system of claim 9 wherein said desiccant is in vapor communication with, but physically separated from, said composition. (Previously presented)

Claim 12 (original): The gas generating system of claim 9 wherein said system is a vehicle occupant protection system. (Previously presented)

Claim 13 (currently amended): A composition comprising: an alkali metal chlorate as an oxidizer provided at about 25-75 weight percent; a carboxylic acid as a fuel provided at about 25-75 weight percent; and a desiccant provided at about 5-35 weight percent, said percentages stated by weight of the total gas generant composition, wherein said desiccant is selected to enhance the thermal stability of the composition.

Claim 14 (original): The composition of claim 13 wherein said carboxylic acid is selected from tartaric acid and its isomers, DL-tartaric acid, succinic acid, glutamic acid, adipic acid, and mucic acid, and mixtures thereof. (Previously presented)

Claim 15 (original): The composition of claim 13 wherein said alkali metal chlorate is potassium chlorate. (Previously presented)

Claim 16 (currently amended): The composition of claim 13 wherein said desiccant is selected from activated calcium sulfate, silica, zeolite, clay, and calcium oxide, wherein said selection is based on their ability to enhance thermal stability.

Claim 17 (original): The composition of claim 13 wherein said desiccant is zeolite. (Previously presented)

Claim 18 (currently amended): The composition of claim 13 wherein said desiccant is selected to provide a mass differential of about -5.0% to 5.0% after heat aging at 107C for 400 hours, wherein said selection is based on enhancing the thermal stability of the composition.
